title: Does the 'larger models are more steerable' finding also mean larger models are more easily jailbroken via steering?

original_idea.body: Within one open model family (Qwen/Pythia sizes) extract comparable refusal directions and measure jailbreak-via-steering ASR-gain vs model size; controlled scaling curve.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: size-scaling of steering-based jailbreak vulnerability is a defensible medium-horizon concern (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Refusal extraction + ASR across one family, forward passes; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped controlled study with clear success criterion (ASR-vs-size curve) (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public model family, externally runnable scaling study (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Multiple sizes up to 7B inference; single GPU, mid-range.

novelty.reasoning: Scaling pitfalls noted; clean within-family curve partly open; partially addressed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Clean within-family scaling curve may be partly open.
